iterations.narrative:
The enrichment analysis identifies **Eicosanoid synthesis (WikiPathways WP167)** as the overwhelmingly top-ranked pathway (FDR = 0, fold enrichment ≈ 1112×), with five metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717) — all confirmed members. A second highly-enriched cluster anchored on the same five compounds spans leukotriene and NSAID pharmacology pathways (SMPDB), indicating the signal is chemically coherent.

**Driver compounds.** Arachidonic acid sits at the apex of this module. KEGG BFS confirms it is a direct precursor of 5-HETE (arachidonic acid → 5-HPETE → 5-HETE) and of 15-HETE (via the 15-lipoxygenase route), and sits in a bidirectional relationship with leukotriene A4 (arachidonic acid → LTA₄ via the 5-lipoxygenase pathway). These two-hop verified paths (length = 2) support arachidonic acid as the key upstream driver. The three HETEs and LTA₄ are therefore likely downstream effectors whose accumulation reflects either increased enzymatic flux or altered lipoxygenase activity in the treatment arm.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of multiple eicosanoids derived from arachidonic acid is a hallmark of inflammatory or oxidative-stress activation. 5-HETE and LTA₄ are potent chemoattractants for neutrophils; 15-HETE and 15d-PGJ₂ carry anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving roles. A simultaneous increase across the spectrum can indicate a feedback attempt to resolve inflammation, or a broader perturbation of membrane phospholipase A₂ availability. The presence of 15d-PGJ₂ — a cyclopentenone prostaglandin with PPARγ-agonist activity — further hints at cross-talk with lipid-sensing nuclear receptors.

Methylmalonic acid (C02170), linked to Vitamin B12 metabolism, is not part of eicosanoid synthesis and likely reflects an independent metabolic perturbation (e.g., B₁₂ cofactor insufficiency) rather than a driver of the eicosanoid signal.
